[0] everyday_reading (E): In everyday life two people swap objects at the same moment, hand to hand, and 'b = a' sounds like 'a and b are now the same thing'. Java statements run one at a time, so the first assignment destroys a value unless it was first saved in a temporary.
[1] misconception (M) -> SwapWithoutTemp: wrong rule: a[i] = a[j]; a[j] = a[i]; exchanges the two values. Right rule: A temporary variable must save a[i] before it is overwritten.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> SwapWithoutTemp: Points to LT (three assignments in order, each using current values). Applied unevenly, a student traces the first two steps correctly but uses a's original value in the third, or calls one segment a swap and the other a copy without tracing either. (here mixing in: "a[i] = a[j]; a[j] = a[i]; exchanges the two values")
[3] misconception (M) -> AssignmentExchangesValues: wrong rule: b = a exchanges the values of a and b. Right rule: b = a copies a into b and leaves a unchanged; an exchange needs a temporary variable and three assignments.

[0] names_the_element (N): Variable swap: the three-assignment idiom that exchanges the values of two variables through a temporary variable.
[1] states_the_rule (S): int t = a; a = b; b = t; exchanges a and b. The temporary t must have their type, and the three statements must run in exactly this order.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Step 1 saves a in t. Step 2 overwrites a with b. Step 3 copies the saved value from t into b. Each step reads values left by the previous one.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Starting from a = 1234 and b = 99, the swap ends with a = 99, b = 1234 and t = 1234.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): Each of the three statements changes exactly one variable: first t, then a, then b.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): A swap is three assignments whose order matters, because each one overwrites the old value of its left variable.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Plan: exchange. It is used to reorder two values (make a <= b), and inside sorting and shuffling of arrays. t plays Sajaniemi's temporary role.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> SwapWithoutTemp: Reordering the steps (int t = a; b = t; a = b;) breaks the swap: both variables end up holding a's value. Dropping the temporary breaks it the same way. Running the correct swap twice restores the originals, so a swap is its own inverse.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use the swap when two variables or array elements must exchange values (sorting, shuffling, ordering a pair). It is not needed when you only need a new variable holding the larger value, or when you can compute directly into new variables.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: An assignment overwrites its target, so a value about to be overwritten must be saved first. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Swapping without a temporary (a = b; b = a;) or in the wrong order: both variables end with the same value whenever a != b.
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The temporary must have the type of the values being swapped. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: Using int t to swap doubles: 'possible lossy conversion from double to int'.
